notes: Calibration anchor for the iPhone 13 session captured the same day: identical model, quantisation, regimes, backend and commit, so the two devices are directly comparable. Measured with llama-bench rather than the iOS harness; llama-bench times prefill and decode as separate tests, so the i-th prefill repeat is paired with the i-th decode repeat here - the pairing is a reporting convention, not a single interleaved run. Machine on mains power with active cooling and not quiesced beyond closing foreground applications; thermalState is not exposed to llama-bench on macOS and is recorded as nominal rather than measured, which is the honest limit of this anchor. This is a base M1, not the M1 Pro used by RooflineBench - a lower tier of the same family, reported as such and never as a reproduction of their figures. The comparison that matters: across five consecutive long generations this machine holds decode flat (64.55 tok/s, no downward trend) while the iPhone 13 falls 40.53 -> 30.93 tok/s on the identical workload. A mains-powered, actively cooled machine cannot exhibit the thermal behaviour that defines phone inference, which is why the phone class needs measuring directly instead of by extrapolation.
